records.verificationNote: Read PDL p. 17 by column x-position and confirmed on the rendered page: Jornay PM capsule is the only stimulant in PREFERRED (no PA). Methylphenidate IR/ER generics and Concerta are PREFERRED WITH PA; the rest of the MPH family is NON-PREFERRED (PDL p. 17-18). PA criteria p. 98 list CC/QL for PA items and p. 103 list Jornay PM as preferred with AE and QL; the age limit value for Jornay PM is not printed next to it, so it is not recorded. Controlled substance (CII): quantity limits only as printed; no day-supply rule added. Starting dose 20 mg is the labeled start for Jornay PM. [Sonnet check 2026-11-03: Re-read PDL p. 17 by x-coordinate (PREFERRED x~190, PREFERRED WITH PA x~312, NON-PREFERRED x~438). Jornay PM is the only product in PREFERRED, but it is a niche evening-dose brand, so the pick is now generic methylphenidate ER (generic Concerta, 18 mg), which is Preferred with PA. That PA is diagnosis only (CC): ADHD or the listed sleep/narcolepsy ICD-10 codes, plus a quantity limit (PA criteria p. 98); no step and no age edit is printed for it. Only Jornay PM carries an age edit (value not printed). Non-preferred stimulants need trial and failure of 2 preferred agents (p. 100). Discrepancy: PDL p. 17 prints brand Concerta in the Preferred-with-PA column while PA criteria p. 103 lists it as not preferred. Previous pick Jornay PM 20 mg kept as the no-PA alternative.]

records.verificationNote: Read PDL p. 17: no amphetamine product is PREFERRED without PA. The mixed amphetamine salts IR tablet is PREFERRED WITH PA, the most common lowest-barrier amphetamine, so it is the pick. Restriction text from PA criteria p. 98 (CC block) and p. 101 (Adzenys age limit >= 6 years, quantity limit 1 per day). Starting dose 5 mg labeled for IR mixed salts. Lisdexamfetamine generic capsule and chewable are NON-PREFERRED on PDL p. 17 and are not listed as alternatives. Dose and quantity per label only. [Sonnet check 2026-11-03: Re-read PDL p. 17 by x-coordinate: mixed amphetamine salts IR and ER, dextroamphetamine 5/10/15 mg tablets and Vyvanse are in PREFERRED WITH PA; nothing amphetamine-family is in PREFERRED. The PA is diagnosis only (CC): ADHD or the listed sleep/narcolepsy codes (Vyvanse also binge eating disorder), plus QL; no step. So the claim that every amphetamine needs PA or a step is correct only in that sense: preferred amphetamines need a diagnosis-only PA, non-preferred ones (Adderall tablet, Evekeo, Adzenys, Dexedrine, Zenzedi, 2.5/7.5/20/30 mg dextroamphetamine) need 2 failed preferred agents (p. 100). Discrepancies to confirm: PDL p. 17 prints Adderall XR capsule as Preferred with PA (PA criteria p. 103 says not preferred), and prints generic lisdexamfetamine as NON-PREFERRED while PA criteria pp. 98 and 103 list it as preferred; so no BOGL is recorded for Vyvanse.]
